title: Frugal kernel expert-system for mixed-load routing and prefill/decode biasing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current kernel-selection pipeline runs relatively heavy microbenchmarks and occasionally falls back to a one-size-fits-all kernel. For mixed workloads (some short-chat decodes + occasional long-prefill generations), this leads to suboptimal cost-latency tradeoffs: decode latency can be higher than needed and long prefill throughput is sometimes throttled by kernels tuned for short sequences.

Goal: Build a lightweight, production-safe "frugal" expert system (advisor) that picks kernels per-request or per-session using a two-stage approach: (1) static fingerprinting (model arch, quantization, instance type, seq-len histogram estimate) and (2) a bounded microprobe budget (very small, e.g., 1-3 microbenchmarks on cold sessions) to validate/override the static recommendation. It should bias picks differently for prefill vs decode phases (prefill prefer throughput/occupancy kernels, decode prefer low-latency/conservative memory). Must be <2% added CPU overhead on the host and safe to roll back.

Why unique: Existing autotuners we've tried are either heavy (long profiling windows) or coarse-grained (per-model defaults). This ticket focuses on a minimal, fast decision service designed for mixed, bursty traffic patterns and fast rollouts.
proposal: Design a compact fingerprint vector: {model_size_bracket, quant_type, gpu_arch, recent-seqlen-percentiles, request-mode(prefill|decode|hybrid)} (encoded as 64-bit key)
Implement a microprobe harness that runs <3 short kernel ops (50-200 tokens) in a sandboxed in-process benchmark with strict CPU/GPU timeouts and metrics collection
Build a lightweight ruleset + scoring model (logistic reg) that returns kernel candidates prioritized by expected latency and cost given the fingerprint

Bias selection by phase: when request indicates prefill-heavy, prefer high-throughput kernels; when decode-heavy, prefer minimal-latency kernels; for hybrid, prefer opportunistic kernels with KV cache friendliness
Instrument a path for safe fallback & fast rollback: i) mark candidate selection via headers, ii) record per-request reason, iii) enable remote kill-switch per-model or per-customer
Expose per-candidate confidence and sample rate for continued online exploration (epsilon-greedy style)
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end routing implemented in runtime experimental route (can be toggled per-model)
Median decode p95 latency regression <= +5% compared to baseline for targeted SLAs on A/B traffic
Average token cost decreased by >= 8% on defined mixed workload benchmark suite (mix of short chat and long prefills)
Microprobe CPU overhead < 2% of host baseline in 95th percentile under target load
Rollback and kill-switch validated in staging and runbook written
tasks: Design fingerprint schema and serialization (proto/flatbuffer) - owner: Luca
Implement microprobe harness (sandbox, timeouts, metric emission) - owner: Eng-rt team
Prototype scoring model + ruleset and unit tests - owner: runtime-ml
Integrate selection hook into scheduler (prefill/decode aware) - owner: scheduler team
Create benchmark suite for mixed loads and cost analysis - owner: perf infra
Ship canary behind feature flag and run 2-week experiment with control vs frugal-advisor - owner: SRE + DataSci
Document rollback, observability signals, and runbook - owner: ops
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only on dev cluster for 1 week (smoke + chaos tests)
Canary: 1% of production traffic for 48h, automated rollback on latency spike or error rate increase
Ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over controlled window with continuous monitoring
Full: opt-in per-model, then global if results stable after 2 weeks

notes: Trade-offs: Lightweight advisor trades some global optimality for low overhead and faster safety checks. It intentionally avoids full multi-epoch profiling.
Edge cases: For multi-request sessions that switch from prefill to decode frequently, we will re-evaluate at session boundary only to minimize probe overhead.
Future: If successful, consider adding a compact online forest (Tiny-Tree) to replace logistic reg for slightly better fidelity without much CPU cost.
